results.headline: On 2026-09-11 12:30-16:30 UTC, Fables' keeper fee (measured on-chain; it matches all 1,820 swaps) averaged 43.7 bp and sat at its 60 bp cap 42 % of the time. At the same average fee, the lab's arbitrage model has clim's rule (12 s blocks) losing 9.8 % more to arbitrage than the keeper's fee path. The keeper's edge is its 60 bp cap poke in the same second as the US CPI release (12:30:00 UTC): the gap comes entirely from the next 15 minutes. Delay its pokes by 30 s, or start the window after the 12:30:12 block, and clim's rule loses 5 to 10 % less than the keeper at the same average fee.
results.measured: Keeper fee rebuilt from 86 FeePoked logs in the window (and the poke live at its start) with the hook's verified rule; it matches the fee paid by 1820 of 1820 swaps. Mean 43.66 bp, range 9.48 to 60 bp.
results.atActualFeeLevels: The keeper charged 2.7 times clim's modelled 12 s fee (43.7 vs 16.1 bp). With no volume response in the model a higher fee always lowers ARB ($35.37 vs $56.11 per $1M), so this row cannot say which fee is better for LPs once traders react.
results.equalAverageFee: Lab-only rescale of clim's k to the keeper's mean: 12 s grid, clim loses +9.8 % vs the keeper (+11.6 % inside Fables' 3.5-60 bp bounds); 1 s grid, +3.5 % (+6.0 % inside the bounds). Positive: clim loses more.
results.whatDrivesIt: At 12:30:00 UTC the keeper poked its cap (tx 0x807ce533677bf7466e753fbc0ada65f136a7de4e31cbd7f5699e0ce9f580fd01) while clim's desk read 48 %/yr and charged 5.30 bp; ETH fell from 2468.89 to 2441.53 within a minute, and clim's fee reached 23.14 bp three minutes later. On the equal-average 12 s path the 12:30:12 block alone costs clim $6.25 against $1.55 for the keeper; $4.50 of gap falls between 12:29 and 12:45 and -$1.05 over the rest of the window (total $3.46): outside those minutes clim's rule loses less. clim's backward-looking 15-minute RV, 30 s reports and 12 s latency cannot anticipate a scheduled jump.
results.sensitivity: Differences in ARB at equal average fee, clim vs keeper (negative: clim loses less). Keeper pokes 30 s late: -10.5 % at 12 s, -8.5 % at 1 s. 12 s late: +9.8 % (the 12:30:00 cap poke still covers the 12:30:12 block). Window starting after the print (12:30:24, 12:45, 13:00): -4.8 %, -7.4 %, -7.5 %. Clamped to Fables' 3.5-60 bp bounds, the difference is -9.0 % with the keeper 30 s late but +1.2 %, +1.5 %, +1.8 % on the later starts: inside those bounds clim's shape does not beat the keeper's even without the print.
results.secondWindow: 2026-09-16 16:50-20:50 UTC (FOMC statement at 18:00 UTC): keeper mean 29.8 bp vs clim 10.5 bp (12 s); the rebuilt fee matches 1725 of 1725 swaps. The keeper poked its cap at 17:59:00 UTC, one minute before the statement, and held 54 to 60 bp through the next 15 minutes. At the same average fee clim loses +10.6 % at 12 s (+6.4 % with the keeper 12 s late, -6.3 % 30 s late) and +63.9 % at 1 s, where the 30 s delay does not change the sign (+51.3 %) because the cap was already in place before the statement; at 1 s, $2.67 of the $2.88 gap falls between 17:59 and 18:15.
results.deployedAsIs: Deployed as-is on Robinhood Chain (0.1023 s blocks), clim's shipped rule would charge its 5 bp floor all window (0 % of the time above it), below Fables' 7 bp flat fee. The 12 s and 1 s runs are modelling choices; the right effective block time for a first-come, first-served L2 is unknown.
results.keeperShape: The keeper's fee follows volatility: over 31 days under its current config its fee correlates 0.83 with Binance RV15, with a median of 7 bp below 40 %/yr, 29.4 bp at 80-100 %/yr and its 60 bp cap above 150 %/yr. It pokes mostly on minute boundaries from one externally owned account. Its logic is off-chain and unknown; its cap pokes coincided with the CPI release and came one minute before the FOMC statement, so its cap was in place when each scheduled release hit.
results.doesNotShow: Fables LPs' realized losses (not measured), anything about traders' response to fees, or what clim would do on Robinhood Chain: the clim line is the lab's re-implementation of the desk on Binance-only prices, not CRE output, and the result rests on two 4 h windows.

cpi.what: US CPI for August 2026, released Friday 11 September 2026 at 08:30 ET (12:30:00 UTC)

fomc.what: FOMC statement, released Wednesday 16 September 2026 at 2:00 p.m. EDT (18:00:00 UTC)

window.whyChosen: Highest 4 h mean Binance RV15 since the ETH/USDG keeper's first poke (2026-08-23T18:19:01Z) and rank 2 since 2026-07-01 (146.9 %/yr mean, peak 445.6 at 2026-09-11T14:04:00Z), in a scan of Binance ETHUSDT 1-minute closes from 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z through 2026-10-07T08:37:00Z (last candle open; lab/scripts/fables_windows.py, lab/out/fables-windows.json). The keeper was live and the current config (100/700/6000 pips) applied. It starts at the US CPI release (12:30:00 UTC).
window.rv15Convention: RV15 at t = sqrt(sum of the 15 squared 1-minute log returns of the 16 minute closes up to t / 900 s), annualized over 365 days; t on minute boundaries in (start, end]

fables.hookContract: FablesRampETH (Sourcify full match; rule in src/base/FablesBaseHook.sol _resolveFee, src/FablesRamp.sol _autonomousFee)
fables.keeperCheck: sender of all 150 FeePoked transactions in the two windows (eth_getTransactionByHash on https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com); eth_getCode of the sender returns 0x
fables.rule: fee = flat; if a poke is live (expiry > block.timestamp): fee = max(pokeFee, floorPips, flat * 5000 / 10000); fee = min(fee, cap). Pokes apply from their block; events ordered by (block, transactionIndex, logIndex).

swapCheck.method: Swap.fee (last data word) of every PoolManager Swap log on the pool vs the rule rebuilt from FeePoked/PoolConfigured at the swap's place in the chain (block, transactionIndex, logIndex). State reads at past blocks are not available (no archive RPC: the public RPC serves no historical state and the Etherscan proxy eth_call ignores the block tag); Swap.fee is the fee each swap actually paid.

caveats: The Fables fee is measured; clim's fee is a model result. The Fables fee is rebuilt from FeePoked and PoolConfigured logs and matches the fee paid by 1820 of 1820 swaps in the window (1725 of 1725 on 2026-09-16). clim's desk did not exist on 2026-09-11 and never ran on Robinhood Chain: the clim line is the lab's Python re-implementation of the desk (RV15 on Binance-only 1 s ETHUSDT prices, RiskDesk envelope, 30 s reports, 12 s latency), not CRE output, standing in for the live four-venue median (Coinbase RV15 mean on this window: 145.8 %/yr vs Binance 146.9 %/yr). CRE lists Robinhood Chain as Robinhood Testnet only (CRE docs as of 2026-09-18, README Roadmap), so neither clim nor CRE runs on Robinhood Chain mainnet today.

Block time: clim's shipped parameters assume 12 s blocks (Ethereum); Robinhood Chain ran at 0.1023 s per block in this window. Deployed as-is on Robinhood Chain, clim would charge its 5 bp floor throughout, below Fables' flat 7 bp: the formula leaves the floor only above 495 %/yr and the window peaked at 446 %/yr (mean fee 5.00 bp). The 12 s and 1 s runs are modelling choices; the right effective block time for a first-come, first-served L2 is unknown. No row here says clim would protect Fables LPs better.

ARB model limits: myopic, gas-free arbitrageur, fixed blocks, fee charged on the input, full-range-equivalent depth. The 1.29 to 1.33 observed-to-model ARB ratio (lab/out/summary.json modelSeverityRatio) was measured on 12 s backtests of Binance data and does not transfer to Robinhood Chain's 0.1 s first-come, first-served blocks. No retail flow and no volume response to fees, so a higher fee always lowers ARB: at actual fee levels (keeper 43.7 bp vs clim 16.1 bp mean on the 12 s grid) ARB favours the higher fee and cannot say which policy is better for LPs or traders. Only the equal-average rows (arbChangeVsStaticPct, equalMean, sensitivity) compare the shape of the policies.

The 2026-09-11 result is driven by one scheduled event: the US CPI for August 2026, released Friday 11 September 2026 at 08:30 ET (12:30:00 UTC), per https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm. The keeper's cap poke 0x807ce533677bf7466e753fbc0ada65f136a7de4e31cbd7f5699e0ce9f580fd01 has block timestamp 12:30:00 while clim read 48 %/yr (5.30 bp). Delaying the keeper's pokes by 30 s, or starting the window after 12:30:12, reverses the sign of the equal-average comparison (sensitivity). On 2026-09-16 the keeper's cap was in place a minute before the FOMC statement, so at 1 s a 30 s delay does not reverse it (secondWindow.sensitivity). clim's backward-looking 15-minute RV, 30 s reports and 12 s latency cannot anticipate a scheduled jump: that is a design limit of the rule, not of the data.

The keeper's logic is off-chain and unknown. We observe only its outputs: pokes from one externally owned account (0x1b6a8808e1d26dba66ba11e52997803c43cad429, eth_getCode = 0x), mostly on minute boundaries, with the TTLs listed in pokesInWindow. Its fee tracks volatility (corr 0.83 with Binance RV15 over 31 days, lab/out/fables-windows.json keeperShape), and its cap pokes coincided with the CPI release and came one minute before the FOMC statement (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm). We make no claim about what it targets.

Robinhood Chain orders transactions first-come, first-served by arrival at the sequencer, with no fee priority (https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/#predictable-transaction-ordering), so its arbitrage dynamics differ from Ethereum's.

Two 4 h windows, not a statistical result. The ARB model ran on 2026-09-11 and 2026-09-16 only; on the other keeper-live windows only the fee levels were compared (lab/out/fables-windows.json topWindows).
Fables LPs' realized losses are not measured: no pool-price-vs-CEX analysis was done.

Pool and price pairs differ: the pool is ETH/USDG, the price is Binance ETHUSDT. On this window Coinbase USDT-USD 1-minute closes stayed within 0.99949-0.99980 (median 0.99965) and the implied USDT/USD from Coinbase ETH-USD over Binance ETHUSDT minute closes had median 0.99971 (range 0.99855-1.00060, close-timing noise included); log returns are unaffected at this level. USDG/USD was not checked.

Launch date: Fables was live on-chain by 2026-08-15T16:31:54Z (PoolManager Initialize at block 37260309, tx 0x043b008deb70ebda2b6a0b78a0db27c824dd4aef3cf675026eec15f4ed9721f3, hooks 0x66622f77b797d506e5376f7798b67ab288966080 = src/FablesRWA.sol:FablesRWA on Sourcify; earliest per the 2026-10-07 scout scan of PoolManager logs, not re-scanned by this script). The research note's 2026-08-17 is the registry date. The ETH/USDG pool was initialized at block 41259014 (2026-08-20T07:58:27Z).

corrFeeSigma for clim is close to 1 by construction: its fee is a clamped linear function of the sigma it reads, and the quartiles and correlations use that same sigma (RV15 as the hook reads it). For the keeper it measures how closely its pokes track that RV15.
